strings.name: Macky Sall
strings.role: Former President of Senegal and former African Union Chairperson
strings.summary: Macky Sall entered politics after working in geology and the petroleum industry. A former prime minister and National Assembly president, he served as Senegal’s president from 2012 to 2024. He promoted development planning and international financing, while restrictions on dissent, an election postponement and inaccurate fiscal reporting during his presidency drew criticism and scrutiny. He continued participating in international public affairs after leaving office.
strings.coverageNote: Information checked through 18 November 2026; recent personal activity is documented by his 1 November meeting with Egypt’s foreign minister. Presidential and AU chairmanship terms, elections and inaugurations, withdrawal announcements and formal withdrawal, and fiscal audits and individual criminal liability are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: A former President of Senegal and rotating African Union chair, he participated in infrastructure development, development financing and Africa’s international affairs.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth and engineering education
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in Fatick on 11 December 1961. He completed studies at Dakar’s Institute of Earth Sciences in 1988 and further training at France’s École nationale supérieure du pétrole et des moteurs in 1993. His geological and petroleum engineering training should not be described as a doctorate.
strings.facts.f2.label: Earlier public offices
strings.facts.f2.value: He worked at the national oil company PETROSEN before holding ministerial portfolios including energy and interior. He was prime minister under President Abdoulaye Wade from 2004 to 2007, then National Assembly president from 2007 to 2008. These offices were separate from his later presidency.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Development planning and financing
strings.highlights.h1.text: He launched the Plan Sénégal Emergent (PSE) in 2014, pursuing economic transformation, social protection and governance reform while seeking public and private investment. Its 2035 development vision was a policy objective; financing pledges and project outcomes require separate assessment.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Controversies over governance
strings.highlights.h2.text: Human Rights Watch criticized restrictions affecting demonstrators, media and internet access during his presidency. After he left office, the IMF confirmed substantial underreporting of deficits and public debt for 2019–2023. This was a finding about fiscal reporting, not a criminal conviction of Sall personally.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Announces withdrawal from the UN leadership race
strings.timeline.t1.text: Sall publicly announced his withdrawal; IISD’s review of the process dates the formal withdrawal to 20 October. Burundi had nominated him. Candidacy did not constitute appointment as Secretary-General.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Hands the presidency to Bassirou Diomaye Faye
strings.timeline.t2.text: Faye took the oath of office, ending Sall’s two presidential terms. The Constitutional Council had overturned February’s election postponement, and voting eventually took place on 24 March. The election and transfer of power occurred on different dates.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becomes African Union Chairperson
strings.timeline.t3.text: He succeeded Tshisekedi at the AU summit in Addis Ababa and was succeeded by Azali Assoumani on 18 February 2023. This rotating position held by heads of state is distinct from the chairmanship of the African Union Commission.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Wins re-election in the first round
strings.timeline.t4.text: On 5 March, the Constitutional Council confirmed 2,555,426 votes for him, representing 58.26% of valid votes. The final result differed from preliminary figures. His second presidential term lasted five years.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Referendum approves constitutional reform
strings.timeline.t5.text: The reforms included shortening presidential terms from seven to five years. Following the Constitutional Council’s opinion, Sall completed his first seven-year term in 2019; the reform did not shorten that term retroactively.
strings.timeline.t6.title: First takes office as president
strings.timeline.t6.text: He was sworn in after defeating Wade in the March presidential election, becoming Senegal’s fourth president. His earlier service as prime minister and parliamentary speaker did not count as presidential terms.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Founds the Alliance for the Republic
strings.timeline.t7.text: After breaking with Wade and the Senegalese Democratic Party, he founded the Alliance for the Republic (APR) and entered opposition politics. Establishing the party was separate from winning the national presidency in 2012.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Becomes Senegal’s prime minister
strings.timeline.t8.text: After earlier ministerial service, he headed the government until 2007, then became National Assembly president. The prime minister led the government; Wade remained the country’s president.
